title: Undo drawer: Boss receipt
summary: A nonnegative event pushes that value onto a stack. A negative event removes up to abs(event) values from its top. Produce the final stack from bottom to top. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
An experimental filing machine records both new cards and requests to undo recent cards. Ivo adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

A nonnegative event pushes that value onto a stack. A negative event removes up to abs(event) values from its top. Produce the final stack from bottom to top.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement undoDrawerBossReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Stack history. A nonnegative event pushes that value onto a stack. A negative event removes up to abs(event) values from its top. Produce the final stack from bottom to top. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with stack history. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

A nonnegative event pushes that value onto a stack. A negative event removes up to abs(event) values from its top. Produce the final stack from bottom to top. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.
